title: `.compile` throws `ValueError: Could not interpret optimizer identifier: <keras.src.optimizers.adam.Adam object at 0x7f419cfc5010>`

Hi @reporter,
I looked into the error you encountered and it appears that you are using `tf_keras==2.20.1`. Since your model was likely built on the `tf_keras` API and not the older `tensorflow.keras` API, there might be an issue when importing `Adam` from `tensorflow.keras.optimizers`. 

To resolve this, try to ensure that the `tf_keras` version you are using matches the version of `tensorflow.keras` that your model was built on.

Let me know if this helps!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Hi @reporter, I think the problem is likely coming from the recent `transformers` migration. HuggingFace moved all their TF models (like DistilBERT) to the standalone`tf_keras` package, not the built-in `tensorflow.keras`.

So, the HF models are now built internally with things like:

```
tf_keras.layers.*
tf_keras.optimizers.*
```   
[HuggingFace docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/installation#tensorflow-support)
check this [guide](https://keras.io/keras_hub/api/models/distil_bert/distil_bert_text_classifier/) mentions that `tensorflow.keras` is the older Keras 2 API that's just kept around for backward compatibility.

For this the serialization is breaking because it is mixing calls from both `tf_keras` (which the HF model uses) and `tensorflow.keras`.
So, it's better to use `tf_keras` everywhere to match the HF models, that should solve the `ValueError` issue.
